title: Choose and insert the missing jigsaw piece
instruction: Complete the jigsaw puzzle by choosing and inserting the correct missing piece.
context: Finishing a jigsaw means checking a candidate two ways at once: does its picture continue its neighbours', and do its tabs and sockets interlock with theirs. Of four candidates, one matches only in shape, one only in picture, one in neither, so neither cue alone picks the right piece, and the right piece fits only one way round.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); turns counterclockwise seen from above. A dark grey base board (20 x 20 x 0.4 cm) is taped to the table centred at x 30, y 0. On it, a 4 x 4 jigsaw (44 mm cells, 17.6 cm square) of 6 mm plywood pieces (top edges chamfered 2 mm, a routed edge) with a printed landscape (sky, sun, grey hills, a red house, a tree, a green meadow and a blue river), upright when seen from the robot's side. Inner edges join with round-headed tabs (a 7 mm neck, a 12 mm head centred 8 mm past the edge, set up to 4 mm off the edge's middle) and matching sockets; pieces are 1.6 mm apart everywhere. 15 pieces are glued to the base; the piece in the second row from the robot and the second column from the robot's right (centre x 27.8, y -2.2) is missing, its hole showing the base. The hole's neighbours toward and away from the robot have tabs into it; its left and right neighbours have sockets. Four loose pieces (8 g each, a 12 mm square, 14 mm tall pine peg glued at the centre of each, the bottom edge bevelled 2 mm in over 2.5 mm up) lie flat on the table, cut to the hole's cell: piece_a at x 25, y 17.5, turned 200 degrees (the right picture, the wrong tabs: tabs away from the robot and to its left, sockets toward it and to its right); piece_b at x 35, y 17.5, turned 70 degrees (the right shape, the picture of the piece to the hole's right); piece_c at x 35, y -17.5, turned 125 degrees (the missing piece); piece_d at x 25, y -17.5, turned 320 degrees (three tabs and the right picture upside down). Turns are from the way each would sit in the hole. Every outline and picture is in pieces.json and print_and_cut.svg.
scoring: Measured at the end of the run with a top photo and a ruler. 0 if a wrong piece (a, b or d) lies in or on the hole (its centre within 1.5 cm of the hole's, its underside within 1.8 cm of the base). Otherwise: 1.0 if the missing piece (c) is seated: its centre within 2.5 mm of the hole's, turned within 5 degrees of the way it fits, flat on the base (underside within 1.5 mm of it, tilted 3 degrees at most), at rest for 1 s. 0.5 if the missing piece lies over the hole but is not seated (centre within 1.5 cm of the hole's, underside within 1.8 cm of the base: resting on its neighbours, turned the wrong way, or not pushed home). 0 otherwise.
reset_notes: Lift the loose pieces by their pegs and lay each on its table mark at its starting turn (marks and turns in the setup screenshot).
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The base and the 15 glued pieces are fixed, each one exact triangle-mesh collider (outline, sides and chamfered top edge); the four loose pieces are free (friction 0.6), each split into strictly convex prisms along its exact outline (a polygon with 20-segment circles), bevelled underneath (2 mm in over 2.5 mm up). With the board's chamfered edges this makes a funnel: checked in PyBullet (check_physics.py), the missing piece let go up to 4 mm off the hole's centre seats every time, and no wrong piece or wrong turn seats. The picture is a coloured print 0.2 mm thick on each piece's flat top, visual only.
